name: Working with School-Age Children and Adolescents
category: Family Studies, Raising and Caring for Children
subject: Social Sciences and Humanities
description: This course prepares students for occupations involving school-age children and adolescents. Students will study a variety of theories about child behaviour and development, and will have opportunities for research and observation and for practical experiences with older children. Students will become familiar with occupational opportunities and requirements related to working with older children and adolescents. They will develop research skills used in investigating child and adolescent behaviour and development.
prerequisites: Any university, college, or university/college preparation course in social sciences and humanities, English, or Canadian and world studies

overall_expectations.title: Issues and Challenges
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of a variety of strategies for helping school-age children and adolescents deal with issues and challenges
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of a variety of strategies for helping school-age children and adolescents deal with issues and challenges

specific_expectations.text: describe skills caregivers teach (e.g., self-advocacy skills, stress-management skills, self-defence skills, social skills for making and keeping friends) and strategies they use (e.g., providing appropriate physical/mental-health support) to help children and adolescents address particular issues and challenges
specific_expectations.text_html: describe skills caregivers teach (e.g., self-advocacy skills, stress-management skills, self-defence skills, social skills for making and keeping friends) and strategies they use (e.g., providing appropriate physical/mental-health support) to help children and adolescents address particular issues and challenges

specific_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of the posi­tive and negative effects of media on children and adolescents (e.g., positive effects such as enhancing awareness of current events, facilitating social connection through social networking; negative effects such as legitimizing violence, pressuring viewers to purchase fad items, increasing opportuni­ties for cyber-bullying)
specific_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of the posi­tive and negative effects of media on children and adolescents (e.g., positive effects such as enhancing awareness of current events, facilitating social connection through social networking; negative effects such as legitimizing violence, pressuring viewers to purchase fad items, increasing opportuni­ties for cyber-bullying)

specific_expectations.text: identify specific challenges faced by people who work with school-age children and ado­lescents, and describe effective strategies for addressing them (e.g., strategies for engaging children with exceptionalities, supporting children living in poverty, responding sensitively and appropriately to diversity)
specific_expectations.text_html: identify specific challenges faced by people who work with school-age children and ado­lescents, and describe effective strategies for addressing them (e.g., strategies for engaging children with exceptionalities, supporting children living in poverty, responding sensitively and appropriately to diversity)

elaborations.text: If a childcare worker suspected that somebody in his after-school program had an eating disorder, what strategies might he use to support the child and her family?
elaborations.text_html: • If a childcare worker suspected that somebody in his after-school program had an eating disorder, what strategies might he use to support the child and her family?

overall_expectations.title: Neglect and Abuse
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of the responsibilities of people who work with school-age children and adolescents in dealing with issues related to abuse, neglect, and family violence
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of the responsibilities of people who work with school-age children and adolescents in dealing with issues related to abuse, neglect, and family violence

specific_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of factors that can lead to patterns of neglect or physical, sexual, or emotional abuse (e.g., a family history of violence, stress, alcoholism)
specific_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of factors that can lead to patterns of neglect or physical, sexual, or emotional abuse (e.g., a family history of violence, stress, alcoholism)

specific_expectations.text: identify indicators of neglect and physical, sexual, or emotional abuse in children (e.g., physical signs such as bruising and laceration; emotional signs such as withdrawal or unexplained fears)
specific_expectations.text_html: identify indicators of neglect and physical, sexual, or emotional abuse in children (e.g., physical signs such as bruising and laceration; emotional signs such as withdrawal or unexplained fears)

specific_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding that people who work with school-age children and ado­lescents have a duty to report suspected cases of neglect or physical, sexual, or emotional abuse, and describe procedures for doing so
specific_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding that people who work with school-age children and ado­lescents have a duty to report suspected cases of neglect or physical, sexual, or emotional abuse, and describe procedures for doing so

elaborations.text: What are the procedures for reporting suspected abuse?
elaborations.text_html: • What are the procedures for reporting suspected abuse?

specific_expectations.text: describe strategies caregivers can use to anticipate and prevent neglect and physical, sexual, and emotional abuse (e.g., education, communication, policy development, advocacy)
specific_expectations.text_html: describe strategies caregivers can use to anticipate and prevent neglect and physical, sexual, and emotional abuse (e.g., education, communication, policy development, advocacy)

overall_expectations.title: Social and Cultural Variations
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of how a variety of social and cultural factors affect school-age children and adolescents
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of how a variety of social and cultural factors affect school-age children and adolescents

specific_expectations.text: describe local and global variations in family forms (e.g., extended families, families led by same-sex partners, polygamous families)
specific_expectations.text_html: describe local and global variations in family forms (e.g., extended families, families led by same-sex partners, polygamous families)

specific_expectations.text: explain how a variety of global challenges (e.g., war, famine, AIDS, use of child labour, natural disasters) affect the lives of children and adolescents
specific_expectations.text_html: explain how a variety of global challenges (e.g., war, famine, AIDS, use of child labour, natural disasters) affect the lives of children and adolescents

elaborations.text: For a teenager whose childhood was spent in a war-torn country, what are some possible effects of that experience on her social development?
elaborations.text_html: • For a teenager whose childhood was spent in a war-torn country, what are some possible effects of that experience on her social development?

specific_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of how expectations related to the behaviour and treatment of children and adolescents vary or have varied in different cultures and historical periods (e.g., up to the industrial period in Western countries, adolescents were viewed as adults)
specific_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of how expectations related to the behaviour and treatment of children and adolescents vary or have varied in different cultures and historical periods (e.g., up to the industrial period in Western countries, adolescents were viewed as adults)

specific_expectations.text: describe strategies and activities that can be used in formal and informal settings to ensure that environments for children and adolescents are free from bias and respectful of diversity
specific_expectations.text_html: describe strategies and activities that can be used in formal and informal settings to ensure that environments for children and adolescents are free from bias and respectful of diversity

elaborations.text: How would you choose materials to put on the walls of a before-school and after-school centre to ensure that the chil­dren in the centre can see themselves reflected in the environment?
elaborations.text_html: • How would you choose materials to put on the walls of a before-school and after-school centre to ensure that the chil­dren in the centre can see themselves reflected in the environment?

specific_expectations.text: compare various forms of childcare in different cultures (e.g., extended families, kibbutzim)
specific_expectations.text_html: compare various forms of childcare in different cultures (e.g., extended families, kibbutzim)

specific_expectations.text: identify various organizations in the community that provide support to families (e.g., children’s aid societies, Dietitians of Canada, police, newcomers’ support centres, family counselling agencies, Native friendship centres, breakfast programs)
specific_expectations.text_html: identify various organizations in the community that provide support to families (e.g., children’s aid societies, Dietitians of Canada, police, newcomers’ support centres, family counselling agencies, Native friendship centres, breakfast programs)
